appendices.B glossary:
Glossary

already there: the same mark was found at pickup within tau_pre of its return position (rule L3).
needs your eye: a human should look; the pair sat in the band between tau_pre and tau_eye, or a cap (K1 to K15) applied (L4).
new or unseen: a return mark with no pickup mark near it; new, or not filmed at pickup (L2).
not seen at return: a pickup mark with no return mark near it (L1).
not comparable: a panel gate failed (G1, G3 to G10); both best frames still show with the reason (L6).
view flagged: Muse Spark said a frame shows water, dirt or glare. That is a model's judgment, so it no longer blocks a panel (gate G2 did that until Oct 31). A mark seen in one walk only is capped at needs your eye (K15); a mark in the same place in both walks keeps its label, with a note.
tight pair: a pair inside tau_pre is already there because the mark sits in the same place in both walks, whatever Muse Spark called it. So Spark's type (dirt, reflection or unsure, K4), the two types disagreeing (K5) and its low confidence (K12) are notes on that pair, and the second look compares the two crops and may lower it (K7). If the second look gives no answer, K4, K5 and K12 cap the pair at needs your eye as before. A mark seen in one walk only, or a pair in the band, keeps them as caps.
keyframe pair: each panel is compared on one pickup keyframe and one return keyframe. When that pair fails a gate of the pair (G3, G4, G5, G8 or G9), the panel's other keyframe pairs are tried in a fixed order (clean views first, then the two keyframe scores, then keyframe number) and the first that passes every gate is used. The panel page says which pair was used and what each pair tried failed. G1, G6, G7 and G10 belong to the panel, so no other pair can pass them.
outline changed in place: a panel that fails only the mask IoU gate (G4) on every keyframe pair tried, with the best IoU from 0.5 to under 0.7, is needs your eye (L7) instead of not comparable when the two keyframes' box shapes agree within 2% and the outline difference sits in one place (its largest blob holds at least half of it). A turned camera changes the box shape or spreads the difference along the whole outline; a crushed panel does neither. No marks are compared, so it never says already there or new.
counter-look: a mark seen in one walk only would be new or unseen (or not seen at return) on distance alone. If no cap already lowers it, the second look is shown the mark in its own walk and the other walk's view of the same panel with the spot where it would sit outlined (carried through the panel frame), and answers two questions: is there a damage mark (scratch, scuff, chip, dent, crack) in the box around the mark, and does the other walk show the same mark at the spot. The label stands only when it says yes to the first and no to the second. Anything else is needs your eye: K17 (the second look saw no damage in the box) when the first answer is no or unsure, K16 (the other walk may show it) when the second is yes or unsure. If it gives no answer, the label stands. A model can only lower a label.
factory fixture: parking sensors, badges, door handles and locks, washer nozzles, the tire valve, the wheel hub and the plate corners are part of the car, not damage. Muse Spark is asked not to box them, and a mark whose box still sits mostly on one the run found in the same view (a point Muse Spark named, or the door handle SAM found) is left out of matching. It gets no label; the panel page names it under how it was checked.
registration: on a compared panel the pickup crop is mapped onto the return crop from the panel's outline (the two SAM masks) and, where there are enough, matched edges of its rigid parts; the fit is refused when the outlines disagree. Each mark's box is then carried to the other crop and the two patches are compared pixel by pixel. If the other walk shows the same patch there and has no mark there, the mark is not new or gone: needs your eye (K18). If it has an unmatched mark there, the two are paired and measured at that spot. Nothing here is a model's answer, and a refused fit changes nothing.
glass: the windshield and rear window get one line, check by eye. Reflections of trees, sky and buildings move with the camera and Muse Spark boxes them as marks, so marks on glass are not compared. The boxes it drew there are kept and counted on the line.
debris: on a compared panel, the needs-your-eye lines whose every mark Muse Spark typed dirt, on a view it flagged wet, dirty or glare, become one line for the panel, debris on this panel; check by eye. A line holding a mark typed as damage or unsure stays as its own line.
colour on the paint: Muse Spark is also asked to box a stripe or patch of a clearly different colour on the paint, such as paint transferred from another car, tape or a sticker, as a scuff. The second look counts one as a mark in the box.
inside the other walk's box: a mark seen in one walk only whose box lies at least half inside a box Muse Spark drew in the other walk's view (often one large box, such as a crush, dirt or a reflection) is not called new or gone, since the other walk did not show clean paint there: needs your eye (K19).
stands out: a mark seen in one walk only must stand out from the paint around it in its own crop, in plain pixels, to be called new or not seen at return. A box that does not (Muse Spark may have boxed clean paint) is needs your eye (K20). A box covering much of its panel, such as a crush, is not tested.
registration vouches: gate G4 asks whether the two walks' views show the same part of the panel by comparing SAM's two outlines. When no keyframe pair passes every gate and G4 is the only gate one fails, a strong registration of the two crops on matched edges (many matched points spread over the panel, small error) shows it directly, and the panel is compared on that pair. A weak or refused fit leaves G4 as it is.
majority look: the second look's answers vary from one ask to the next, so the pair look (K7) and the counter-look (K17 and K16) are asked up to three times, stopping once two answers agree, and the label follows the majority. A split is unsure, so a model can still only lower a label. Every answer is kept.
units: panel-normalized distance; 1 unit is about 35 cm along a door (the about-cm beside it uses that).
tau_pre, tau_eye: the two distance thresholds, calibrated from the run's own repeat frames; printed on the method page.
Stays Put: a check that a mark moves with the panel through a short clip; a reflection slides, a scratch stays put.
sha256: the fingerprint of a file; one changed byte changes it.
sealed: the manifest of hashes was written and offered for time stamping before any model saw the video.
config hash: the fingerprint of every threshold the code used; it changes when a threshold changes.
rule id: the row of the decision table that produced a label; G gates a panel, K caps a mark, L names a label, E is a claim exit.
appendices.C verify it yourself:
Verify it yourself (5 steps; none needs Walkaround's server)

1. Hash the video file on your phone or computer and compare it with page 1:
   shasum -a 256 <your video file>     (Linux: sha256sum <your video file>)
   pickup: 0b1d3a373eeccd030eb8cc1eeadfa408d929a48cbabcf2f90481923bf4eca2cf
   return: cc683f02ad13d63d148fb5568724560f5c35e3d15202edcf7a21609cc23024f3
2. Read the OpenTimestamps proof (pip install opentimestamps-client):
   ots info bundle/manifest.json.ots
3. Verify it against the Bitcoin block, or drop the .ots file on https://opentimestamps.org :
   ots verify bundle/manifest.json.ots
4. Verify the RFC 3161 token from freetsa (2026-11-02T22:13:00Z) with freetsa's certificates (download https://freetsa.org/files/cacert.pem and https://freetsa.org/files/tsa.crt):
   openssl ts -verify -data bundle/manifest.json -in bundle/manifest.json.tsr -CAfile cacert.pem -untrusted tsa.crt
5. Re-hash every file in the bundle and rebuild the derived files from the stored model answers:
   walkaround verify hero_focus4

privacy_line: Processed with Meta's Model API in Standard mode, which Meta's documentation says is not used to train Meta models. Uploads were set to expire after one hour and were deleted by Walkaround when the run ended. Model requests were sent with storage off. SAM 3.1 saw the unblurred proxy for the length of one segmentation pass to find the plates and faces it then blurred. For the second look, two blurred crops per look were sent to Muse Spark Open on Baseten, a company separate from Meta; no video went there.
